captures.stdout:
Wireblast: the iPerf of packet generators.

Generate line-rate traffic from a Linux box using AF_XDP, without knowing
anything about AF_XDP. Run it with no flags for an interactive wizard, or
specify everything and add --no-tui for scripts.

  sudo wireblast
  sudo wireblast -i eth1 --dst-ip 192.0.2.10 --pps 1M --duration 30s --no-tui

Wireblast transmits only by default: it attaches an XDP program that redirects
nothing, so your SSH session and all other receive traffic keep flowing through
the kernel untouched. Receiving through AF_XDP is opt-in via --rx-mode.

--packet-size is the total Ethernet frame size in bytes INCLUDING the 4-byte
FCS, so --packet-size 64 means the classic 64-byte frame.

Bit rates are reported as L1 and L2, the same two T-Rex reports. L1 is the
frame plus its 20 bytes of preamble, start-frame delimiter and interframe gap,
and is what link utilisation means; L2 is the frame itself. --bps is measured
in L1, so --bps 10G means 10G line rate.

Usage:
  wireblast [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-match-all      required acknowledgement for --rx-mode all, which takes EVERY packet from the kernel
      --bps string           bit rate limit in L1 bits (frame plus preamble, SFD and interframe gap), aggregate across queues (e.g. 10G, 2.5Gbps, or 'unlimited')
      --dst-ip string        destination IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR (a CIDR cycles destinations across flows)
      --dst-mac string       next-hop MAC address (default: resolved from the neighbour and routing tables)
      --dst-port uint16      destination port (fixed unless --vary-dst-port) (default 9000)
  -d, --duration duration    how long to transmit (0 = until stopped) (default 30s)
      --ethertype string     EtherType for --mode raw (e.g. 0x88b5)
      --flow-order string    order flows are walked in: sequential, random (default "sequential")
      --flows int            number of distinct flows to generate (1 = a single flow) (default 1)
      --forget               discard the remembered settings from previous runs and start from the defaults
  -h, --help                 help for wireblast
  -i, --interface string     network interface to transmit from (the physical NIC, not a VLAN sub-interface)
  -m, --mode string          traffic pattern: udp, tcp-syn, imix, raw, pcap, receive (default "udp")
      --no-tui               skip the wizard and dashboard; validate the flags and run, printing periodic statistics
  -s, --packet-size int      total Ethernet frame size in bytes, including the 4-byte FCS (default 64)
      --payload-byte int     repeating payload byte value for --mode raw (default 90)
      --pcap string          Ethernet PCAP/PCAPNG file to replay (--mode pcap)
      --pcap-loop            loop the capture until the duration expires (default true)
      --pcap-memory string   memory budget for loading the capture, in binary units (e.g. 512M, 4G; default 1G). The whole capture is held in RAM, so the budget has to fit
      --pcap-timing string   pcap pacing: rate (use --pps/--bps) or original (preserve capture timing) (default "rate")
      --pps string           packet rate limit, aggregate across queues (e.g. 1M, 500k, or 'unlimited')
      --queues int           number of NIC queues to transmit on (0 = all)
      --rx-cidr string       source CIDR for --rx-mode cidr
      --rx-mode string       what to receive through AF_XDP: none, generated-flow, udp-port, tcp-port, cidr, keep-management, all (default "none")
      --rx-port strings      destination port(s) for --rx-mode udp-port/tcp-port (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --src-ip string        source IPv4 or IPv6 address (default: an address of the selected interface)
      --src-mac string       source MAC address (default: the selected interface's MAC)
      --src-port uint16      first source port; incremented per flow (default 1024)
      --start                skip the wizard and start straight away, showing the live dashboard
      --vary-dst-port        also increment the destination port per flow
  -v, --version              version for wireblast
      --vlan int             802.1Q VLAN ID to tag frames with (1-4094; 0 = untagged)
  -y, --yes                  skip ordinary confirmation prompts (does not bypass the --rx-mode all guard)
